description: Add real-time progress feel to the session page: live-ticking duration on running tool rows, a persistent current-activity bar, a block cursor on streaming assistant text, and an elapsed timer on the thinking indicator. Pure presentation layer; consumes the #427 row anchor and the #426 liveness gate.

tasks.title: Live-ticking duration on running tool rows
tasks.description: Introduce the shared ticking clock infrastructure (an injectable `useNow({ intervalMs, now? })` hook in `widgets/session-transcript/model/use-now.ts` and a `formatElapsedNow(startedAt, nowMs)` helper alongside the existing `formatElapsed`) and render a once-per-second ticking elapsed duration on tool rows whose state is `pending` or `running`. Wire `SessionTranscriptLayout` to call `useNow` only while `isRunning` is true and thread the resulting `now` value down to in-progress rows only (terminal rows keep using `formatElapsed` and stay memoizable). On transition to `completed`/`failed`/`cancelled` the displayed duration freezes at the finalized `startedAt → completedAt` delta.
acceptanceCriteria: A `pending` or `running` tool row in a live session renders an elapsed duration that advances once per second, formatted via the existing duration format (e.g. `4.7s`, `2m 03s`)
A `completed`, `failed`, or `cancelled` tool row renders the frozen `startedAt → completedAt` delta and does not change on subsequent ticks
When the session transitions from running to not running mid-tool, the in-progress row's duration stops ticking
A non-running session renders no ticking duration on any row
Only in-progress rows receive the `now` prop; terminal rows are unaffected by per-second re-renders
`useNow` and `formatElapsedNow` unit tests pass with fixed timestamps and `vi.useFakeTimers`; no wall-clock waits or `elapsed < N` assertions
`npm run typecheck -w packages/web` and `npm run test:run -w packages/web` pass
tasks.output: widgets/session-transcript/model/use-now.ts (hook + unit test), widgets/session-transcript/model/format-duration.ts (formatElapsedNow + unit test), ToolRowView ticking duration in tool-views/index.tsx, SessionTranscriptLayout useNow wiring
tasks.notes: This task introduces the shared clock infrastructure that T-002 and T-004 consume. Follow the ActivityPage `now?: number` injection precedent (pages/activity/ui/ActivityPage.tsx:133-161). Per design D2, only pass `now` to in-progress rows so React.memo on ToolRowView stays effective for terminal rows.

tasks.title: Persistent current-activity bar with click-to-jump
tasks.description: Add a `selectActiveToolCall(turns: DisplayTurn[]): DisplayToolPart | null` pure selector and a new `CurrentActivityBar` component rendered inside `SessionTranscriptLayout` as the last child of the scroll content, pinned with `position: sticky; bottom: 0`. The bar shows the active tool's verb-led title and live elapsed duration (reusing T-001's `now` and `formatElapsedNow`), renders only when `isRunning` and an active tool exists, and on activation (click or keyboard) queries the scroll container for `[data-tool-call-id="<activeToolCallId>"]` and calls `scrollIntoView({ block: 'center' })`.
acceptanceCriteria: The bar renders at the bottom of the transcript viewport, remaining visible across all scroll positions, while the session is running and a `pending`/`running` tool call exists
The bar does not render when the session is not running or when no tool call is in progress
The bar is removed when the session ends mid-tool
The bar displays the active tool's title and a duration that ticks once per second
Activating the bar scrolls the tool row whose `data-tool-call-id` matches the active tool call into view
When the active tool transitions to a new call, subsequent activation targets the new call's row
`selectActiveToolCall` unit tests cover: no active tool, single active tool, and deterministic last-match tiebreak
Bar render/gating/click-jump spec tests use mocked `scrollIntoView` and fixed timestamps; `npm run typecheck -w packages/web` and `npm run test:run -w packages/web` pass
tasks.output: widgets/session-transcript/model/select-active-tool-call.ts (selector + unit test), widgets/session-transcript/ui/CurrentActivityBar.tsx (component + spec test), SessionTranscriptLayout bar mounting
tasks.notes: Reuses T-001's useNow call already in SessionTranscriptLayout; consume the same `now` value for the bar's duration. Do not introduce a parallel ref registry — the existing data-tool-call-id anchor from #427 is the lookup key. Sticky positioning cannot be asserted in jsdom; assert presence/absence and the position class, defer true sticky verification to the browser track if needed.

tasks.title: Block cursor on streaming assistant text
tasks.description: Replace the trailing streaming dot glyph in `AssistantTextPartView` with a block cursor (an `inline-block` span rendered after the TranscriptMarkdown output) that appears when `isRunning && (completedAt is null || isStreaming)`. Blinking is via Tailwind's existing `animate-pulse`. The cursor is `aria-hidden="true"`, not focusable, and carries no semantic role.
acceptanceCriteria: An incomplete or actively streaming assistant text part in a live session renders a block cursor at the end of the streamed text
A completed text part renders no block cursor
The block cursor does not render when the session is not running, regardless of the streaming flag
The block cursor is removed when a streaming text part completes or when the session ends mid-stream
The cursor is marked `aria-hidden="true"`, is not focusable, and carries no semantic role
The previous trailing dot glyph (`assistant-text-streaming-glyph`) is removed; the Copy button row remains
Spec tests cover render gating, removal on completion/session-end, and accessibility attributes; `npm run typecheck -w packages/web` and `npm run test:run -w packages/web` pass
tasks.output: widgets/session-transcript/ui/AssistantParts.tsx (AssistantTextPartView block cursor replacing dot glyph + spec test updates)
tasks.notes: Independent of T-001: the cursor uses CSS animate-pulse for blinking and consumes only the already-plumbed isRunning flag and the part's completedAt/isStreaming state. No useNow dependency.

tasks.title: Thinking-elapsed timer on the thinking indicator
tasks.description: Capture the thinking-state start timestamp in `SessionTranscriptLayout` via a ref that records `Date.now()` when `isThinking` transitions from false to true (reset to null when it becomes false). Modify `ThinkingPlaceholder` to receive `now` (from T-001's useNow call) and the captured start, and display the elapsed time formatted via `formatDuration`, ticking once per second. The elapsed display is gated on `isRunning && isThinking`.
acceptanceCriteria: While the session is running and in the thinking state, the thinking indicator displays an elapsed time that advances once per second, formatted via the existing duration format
The thinking elapsed display does not render when the session is not running, regardless of any lingering thinking flag
The thinking indicator and its elapsed display are removed when the session ends
The elapsed display stops advancing or is removed when the agent leaves the thinking state (e.g. visible content begins streaming)
The thinking-start timestamp captures the false→true transition of isThinking and resets on true→false
Spec tests use `vi.useFakeTimers` and fixed timestamps to verify ticking, gating, and removal; no wall-clock waits; `npm run typecheck -w packages/web` and `npm run test:run -w packages/web` pass
tasks.output: widgets/session-transcript/ui/SessionTranscriptLayout.tsx (ThinkingPlaceholder elapsed timer + thinking-start ref capture + spec test)
tasks.notes: Consumes T-001's useNow call already in SessionTranscriptLayout. Per design D7, the thinking-start timestamp is presentation-local (captured via ref on isThinking transition), not a new data-source field. A page reload mid-think resets the timer — acceptable per the issue's live-progress framing.
